## Round 31 Design Spec — Text-Based PEAD (PEAD.txt Methodology)

**Status:** QUEUED (after R28 and R29 complete)
**Inspired by:** PEAD.txt — Meursault, Liang, Routledge & Scanlon, JFQA 2022. Still validated in 2025–2026 citations.
**Source:** https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/journal-of-financial-and-quantitative-analysis/article/peadtxt-post-earnings-announcement-drift-using-text/5EB217BB68B5FB054FE38541BAAC4679

### The Problem R31 Solves
R30 found that 12-quarter elastic net SUE = same Sharpe as single-quarter SUE on 22 large-caps (~1.21–1.22 annualized). The numeric earnings surprise is efficiently priced out for large-caps — the market reacts to the number instantly.

But PEAD.txt shows the TEXT of the earnings call carries orthogonal, under-exploited information:
- **Classic PEAD (SUE):** 2.6 bps/day alpha
- **Text PEAD (SUE.txt):** 3.9 bps/day alpha — 50% stronger
- **Key:** SUE.txt signal PERSISTS in recent years when classic PEAD has decayed to ~0
- **Interpretation:** Markets quickly price numeric surprises but are slow to fully process HOW management explains the results (forward guidance language, hedging language, tone of Q&A)

### Proposed Architecture

**Stage 1 — Earnings Call Transcript Collection:**
- Use Financial Modeling Prep (FMP) API: `/earning_call_transcript` endpoint
- Pull transcripts for all current PEAD tickers (Fortune 100 universe, 2021–2025)
- FMP Premium plan has this; free tier may have recent quarters
- Fallback: Motley Fool transcript archives (web scrape with agent-browser)
- Estimated: ~4 quarters × ~30 tickers = ~120 transcripts

**Stage 2 — Text-Based Surprise (SUE.txt Proxy):**
Approach A — FinBERT scoring (faster, no training needed):
- Segment transcript into paragraphs: Prepared Remarks vs Q&A separately
- Run `ProsusAI/finbert` on each paragraph → positive/neutral/negative scores
- Aggregate: transcript_score = weighted avg of paragraph scores (Q&A weighted 1.5x — management responses to analyst probes carry more signal per PEAD.txt)
- Construct 'text surprise': transcript_score - rolling_12Q_avg_score (same concept as SUE: deviation from expected tone)
- High positive text surprise = company sounded materially more optimistic than usual → long signal

Approach B — GPT/Claude rating (slower but richer):
- For each transcript, prompt: 'Rate the management confidence and forward guidance optimism in this earnings call on a scale of 0-100. Focus on: guidance language, response to analyst concerns, language around margin/growth trajectory. Return a single integer.'
- Use as ordinal ranking signal
- Higher API cost but potentially captures narrative nuance FinBERT misses

**Recommended:** Start with Approach A (FinBERT, no API cost, fast). Use Approach B as a comparison on the same subset.

**Stage 3 — PEAD.txt Backtest:**
- Event dataset: reuse existing 80+ PEAD events from R26/R28 backtest (same tickers, dates)
- Entry signal: text_surprise > 0 (positive deviation from historical tone baseline)
- Optional threshold: text_surprise > 0.10 (top tercile only)
- Hold: 20–40 days (same as best PEAD holds from prior rounds)
- Comparison arms:
  1. Classic PEAD (SUE > 3%) — Sharpe ~2.394 from R26
  2. PEAD.txt standalone (text surprise only)
  3. PEAD combined: both SUE > 3% AND text_surprise > 0 (requires both signals)
  4. PEAD.txt as exit sentinel: hold PEAD until negative text surprise (FinBERT < -0.70 threshold from FinBERT exit sentinel heuristic)

### Data Sources
- Transcripts: FMP API (`https://financialmodelingprep.com/api/v3/earning_call_transcript/AAPL?quarter=3&year=2023&apikey=KEY`)
- FinBERT: `pip install transformers`, model `ProsusAI/finbert`
- Existing PEAD event dates: `/workspace/group/trading_eval/rounds/pead_results.json`

### Cost Estimate
- FinBERT: $0 (local inference, ~2 min/transcript on CPU)
- FMP transcripts: ~$0.01–0.05/transcript if on paid plan; check free tier limits
- Total: ~$5 for data if FMP paid plan; potentially free if using Approach B with existing PEAD event dates only

### Success Criteria
- PEAD.txt standalone Sharpe > classic PEAD Sharpe (2.394) → text signal adds independent value
- Combined PEAD (SUE + text) Sharpe > either alone → signals are complementary
- If PEAD.txt < classic PEAD: record that text signal doesn't transfer in our large-cap universe (document as finding)

### Connection to Heuristics
- Per FinBERT exit sentinel lesson (heuristics.md): high FinBERT threshold as EXIT control (not entry) → consider Arm 4 above
- Per LLM-as-narrator lesson: Approach B (Claude scoring) may be more valuable as narrative label for product features than as raw alpha signal

### R31 Dependency Note
R31 can proceed in parallel with or after R28/R29 since it uses different data and a different signal source. No blocking dependency.
